fields.place: Kerala (temples at Kraṅganore and Kulaśekharapuram; maṭha at Kumbakonam)
fields.works: Mukunda-mālā-stotra (53 verses; quoted in CC Madhya 13.78 and Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu 2.6.29); Tamil hymns in the Nālāyira Prabandham (if he is the Ālvār)
fields.notes: King of Kerala, patron of Vaiṣṇavism in the South before Śaṅkara; built temples and a maṭha; author of the Mukunda-mālā-stotra. Probably the same as the Ālvār Kulaśekhara of the Tamil Prabandham, though some scholars distinguish them.

fields.name: Jagadeva Pramāra
fields.notes: An honest, renounced Vaiṣṇava of the Bhaktamāla. Refused a princess's hand; overwhelmed by a singer's Harināma, cut off his head and offered it to him; the head kept turning away from the princess, who put it back on his body, and he revived and married her; later he renounced home (Bhaktamāla; Viśvakoṣa).

Kāyastha official of King Gaṇeśa of Gauḍa; after Gaṇeśa's son became Jalāluddīn he made himself king of Pāṇḍuā, sheltering Gaṇeśa's Hindu ministers; Padmanābha (ancestor of Rūpa and Sanātana) settled in his land at Naihāṭī. Driven out by the Pathans, founded the kingdom of Candradvīpa (Bāklā). Coins of 1417-18 bear his name.
